title: Machine learning predicts postpartum depression from electronic health records
summary: A machine-learning framework selected a minimal feature list from health records of 15,197 women at one site, and was validated on 53,972 women across multiple sites. AUC was 0.937 (95% CI 0.912-0.962) in development and 0.886 (0.879-0.893) in validation, and results held when data ended at different points in pregnancy. The outcome reflects diagnosed treatment prevalence, which is likely lower than illness prevalence.
ai_technology: Machine-learning framework on electronic health record features

evidence.tested: Performance was evaluated on an independent multisite dataset, at several time points during pregnancy.
evidence.unknown: The algorithm is not named in the abstract; effect on prevention is not tested. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning framework selected features and predicted diagnosis within a year of childbirth.
